newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel gets go-ahead for passenger trains.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel gets go-ahead for passenger trains.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc/SA got the go-ahead on Tuesday to reopen the Channel tunnel railway to passenger services, including the Eurostar inter-city express trains and tourist vehicle shuttles, whenever they are ready.

After a key safety committee meeting in London, the Inter- Governmental Commission (IGC) of French and British government representatives said the tunnel, which was closed after a fire in the tunnel two weeks ago, could now be reopened.

Eddie Ryder, head of the British delegation for the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority, said: "It (the authority) is now satisfied that the necessary safety equipment is available and that revised operating and emergency procedures are in place."
However, Ryder said the heavy goods vehicle shuttles could only resume after the completion of a French investigation into the causes of the fire, which started on such a vehicle.

The tunnel has been closed to all passenger traffic since November 18, when a fire on a truck destroyed a freight shuttle train and severely damaged a 300 metre section of the tunnel, injuring 34 people.
Eurotunnel staged a drill on Sunday to prove that it could safely run passenger services when one of the two rail tunnels is still closed for repairs.
